newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * President Emil Constantinescu meets opposition leaders to discuss parliamentary support for the government's reform package.

* Adrian Nastase, leader of the main opposition Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) said the president should invite all parties in parliament. He said the PDSR is against the government's plans to put the State Ownership Fund (FPS) under its control.

* Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will meet the managers of state-run Petromidia refinery this afternoon. Petromidia is one of two refineries on a government list of companies to be liquidated under a tough reform programme.
Petromidia managers want to persuade Ciorbea that the refinery does not have debts to the state budget and is still attractive for foreign investors.
* The ruling National Peasant Party backs a government decision to take control of the FPS, the party's secretary general Radu Vasile said.
Vasile said Romania's signing the accord to join CEFTA was very important for the country's bid to become a member of the European Union.
* Romania's exiled King Michael is in the Netherlands, on a tour of European parliamentary monarchies, to lobby for Romania's first-wave NATO admission bid.
* Romania's special envoy toi London, parliamentarian Ion Ratiu, met British Foreign Office officials to discuss support for Romania's early NATO membership bid.
Ratiu said that the Foreign Office declined to express a position on the issue until Britain's general elections in May.
* The Canadian ambassador to Bucharest said Ottawa strongly supports Romania's bid to join NATO among first-wave entrants.
* The Black Sea ports of Constanta, Mangalia and Midia were closed due to strong winds.
